summary: The Gambia's NDC pledges span agriculture, restoration, conservation, and mixed land-use actions. In agriculture, the country targets 30,000 ha of methane-reducing rice management, 150,000 ha of zero/minimum tillage, and 50,000 ha of cover crops by 2035, plus 95,000 ha of multistrata agroforestry; these area pledges cover about 48% of current agricultural land. Restoration commitments include reforesting 80,000 ha and establishing 75,000 ha of agroforestry/restoration systems by 2035, equivalent to about 45% and 42% of current forest cover, respectively. Conservation aims to protect 72,000 ha of forest from deforestation/degradation (≈41% of forest cover). Additional quantified GHG reductions include 205, 408, 169, 169, and 373 GgCO2e for climate-smart agriculture, livestock, agroforestry, firewood, and re-greening degraded landscapes.
